teams.synopsis: Two weeks on top, but a double bye from Ekeler and Kelce could slow the roll.
teams.blurb: The top team for two weeks in a row might take a step back this week with <mark class="hl-player">Ekeler</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Kelce</mark> on bye. This team is almost a lock for the playoffs but still needs a couple of wins under its belt to secure a playoff bid.

teams.synopsis: Consistently near the top — Jacobs is playing like a top-5 back even with Njoku out.
teams.blurb: A consistent team that remains at the top of the standings — Root's team continues to shine with <mark class="hl-player">Jacobs</mark> looking like a top-5 running back. The loss of <mark class="hl-player">Njoku</mark> at TE might hinder this team's production, but I still expect a top-5 finish every week.

teams.synopsis: Losing Mike Williams stings, but Swift's return keeps this team humming.
teams.blurb: The loss of <mark class="hl-player">Mike Williams</mark> might have this manager annoyed and wondering how his team will continue to perform at an elite level, but with the return of <mark class="hl-player">Swift</mark>, I think Malich can keep up his showing of brilliance. On a side note, this team is actively looking for trade partners, so be ready for a big one.

teams.synopsis: Losing a top-10 RB hasn't slowed this team down — still projected as a top-3 finisher.
teams.blurb: RIP <mark class="hl-player">Breece</mark>. This team is still very competitive even with the loss of one of his top-10 RBs. I project Ryan to finish as a top-3 team by the end of the year and be in contention for PFFL champion.

teams.synopsis: Two strong weeks finally earn this team a spot in the top five.
teams.blurb: Finally making the big jump — I decided this team has earned a spot in the top five because of their play the past two weeks, and the possibilities and potential this squad has.

teams.synopsis: Still coasting on that Week 4 explosion, but the talent to keep competing is there.
teams.blurb: He might complain about this spot, but I think it's a perfect placement. In Week 4, Brandon's squad erupted for 177 points, and I think he's been riding that output for the past few weeks. Recently, this team has put up lackluster numbers, but they have the skillset and the players to keep competing for the PFFL playoffs.

teams.synopsis: A rough Week 7, but the James Robinson trade could be the spark this team needs.
teams.blurb: A disappointing Week 7 knocks this team down a spot, but the <mark class="hl-player">James Robinson</mark> trade might provide some life for this team. A very solid receiving corps and a top TE give this team a chance any given week.

teams.synopsis: On the rise, with CMC and CD as the engine — the RB2 and TE spots are the real question marks.
teams.blurb: This team is definitely on the rise, but question marks surround <mark class="hl-player">CMC</mark> and whether he'll be able to produce top-5 RB numbers on SF. The weakness at TE and RB2 doesn't help this team's chances of making a playoff run, but the one-two punch of CMC and <mark class="hl-player">CD</mark> might be enough to win some games.

teams.synopsis: A step forward despite the noise — trades could be coming to lock in a playoff push.
teams.blurb: This team has really taken a step forward in recent weeks, and I think that's due to a multitude of factors — like <mark class="hl-player">Diggs</mark> being on bye, <mark class="hl-player">Brian Robinson</mark> returning from injury, and <mark class="hl-player">Curtis Samuel</mark> being inconsistent as of late. I wouldn't be surprised if Deniz attempts to make a few trades to get his team right and in line to make the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: The unluckiest record in the league — the points are there, the wins just aren't.
teams.blurb: The most unlucky manager this year — Quigley's team seems as if they've given up this season because of the lack of wins, even though they've put up a lot of points. Aidan doesn't have much time to start winning games, and over these next couple weeks he'll have to decide if he's playing to make the playoffs or just to avoid coming in last.

teams.synopsis: A 3-of-4 stretch has this cellar-dweller quietly building a sneaky playoff case.
teams.blurb: One of the lowest-ranked teams all season, it seems like Quin's team has been picking it up as of late, though. Winning 3 of his last 4 is an impressive feat and might mean brighter days are ahead for this squad. Maybe we're in store for a sneaky playoff run from Geg??

teams.synopsis: Elite at WR and QB, shaky at RB — Fournette and Melvin Gordon need to answer the bell.
teams.blurb: A team that's continued to underperform. Ben's team is led by a top-3 WR duo in the league and <mark class="hl-player">Josh Allen</mark>, but my concern is at the RB position. Will <mark class="hl-player">Fournette</mark> produce consistent RB1 numbers, and will <mark class="hl-player">Melvin Gordon</mark> be fantasy-relevant again this season? If Ben's team continues this downward spiral, we might be watching him run next summer.

teams.synopsis: A rough stretch and a crowded bye schedule — the playoffs look like a longshot from here.
teams.blurb: A fall from grace. Baylen's squad could use a confidence boost. The problem with this team is that <mark class="hl-player">Rhamondre</mark> has taken the starting role from <mark class="hl-player">Harris</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">MT</mark> doesn't play games anymore. With <mark class="hl-player">Herbert</mark> on bye this week and his RBs on bye next week, this team has little to no chance to make a playoff run — but everyone loves an underdog.

teams.synopsis: Last place since Week 3, but a 100-point week hints there's still some fight left.
teams.blurb: The last-place team since Week 3, Maney has been plagued by injuries all season. Last week, however, he scored over 100 points for the first time since Week 4. This team's playoff hopes will most likely be tarnished with a loss this week, if they haven't been already. I'd keep an eye on this team, though — I've seen crazier things happen. With that being said, this squad should really only have one goal for the rest of the season: don't come in last.
